summary: Tested dashboard stats tax calculation fix. The bug was that ICMS, PIS, COFINS were showing as zero in the Dashboard even with R$ 969k+ in NFCe sales. The fix adds a separate aggregation pipeline in _get_dashboard_stats_aggregated to calculate taxes at PRODUCT level (produtos.v_icms, produtos.v_pis, produtos.v_cofins) instead of using non-existent icms_total field. All 15 tests passed.
critical_code_review_comments: FIX VERIFIED: pipeline_impostos correctly uses $unwind on produtos[] and sums v_icms, v_pis, v_cofins
The fix uses $ifNull to check for both v_icms and valor_icms (fallback) field names
Aggregation pipeline correctly groups by tipo (entrada/saida) for debit/credit calculation
Normal version (<5000 docs) already calculated taxes correctly at product level in Python loop
Both versions now produce consistent results: ICMS is >0 when there are products with v_icms
For NFCe, PIS and COFINS are typically 0 in the XML (tributação monofásica) - this is expected behavior
seed_data_creation: None - Used existing test data (test-company-dashboard and Republic company)
context_for_next_testing_agent: Dashboard tax calculation fix verified. Key scenarios tested: 1) Normal version (<5000 docs) with test-company-dashboard, 2) Aggregated version (>5000 docs) with Republic (14,700 docs). Both correctly return ICMS > 0 when products have v_icms values. For NFCe, PIS/COFINS are typically 0 in XML (tributação monofásica).

bug_fix_verification.original_bug: ICMS, PIS, COFINS were showing as zero in Dashboard even with R$ 969k+ in NFCe sales
bug_fix_verification.root_cause: _get_dashboard_stats_aggregated used 'icms_total' field which doesn't exist. Should sum produtos[].v_icms instead.
bug_fix_verification.fix_implemented: Added pipeline_impostos aggregation with $unwind on produtos[] to sum v_icms, v_pis, v_cofins at product level
bug_fix_verification.fix_verified: YES - Both normal and aggregated versions now correctly calculate taxes from product-level fields

rca_of_the_issue: The aggregated version of dashboard stats was using 'icms_total' from document level which doesn't exist or is zero. The correct approach is to $unwind the produtos array and sum the v_icms, v_pis, v_cofins fields from each product. The fix adds a separate pipeline (pipeline_impostos) that does exactly this, ensuring consistent tax calculations for large document sets.
